English: Ember Stand

A simple, makeshift platform of stones and earthen mound, used to protect a single sacred ember. Serves as the most basic holy site for nomadic Zoroastrians, focusing on preserving tradition and unity at the frontier.
Torch Post
A wooden post crowned with burning torches, marking a gathering spot for communal prayers. It expands the ember stand, strengthening clan bonds through shared ritual.
Fire Pit
A carefully-dug pit lined with stones, holding a larger sacred fire for ceremonies. The fire pit enables more elaborate rituals and is a focal point for clan unity.
Flame Pavilion
A large, tented structure with ornate cloth and banners, sheltering the sacred flame. The pavilion allows rituals in any weather and draws more followers to the faith.
Priests Room
A dedicated, partitioned tent or yurt for the resident Mobed (priest), providing space for sacred texts and private meditation. This marks a shift to organized religious leadership.
Altar Chamber
A semi-permanent wooden or stone structure with a raised altar for holy offerings, attended by multiple priests. Rituals now include the whole clan and attract spiritual visitors.
Sanctified Hall
A large, decorated tent or wooden hall adorned with tapestries and symbols of Ahura Mazda. The sanctified hall becomes the spiritual heart for many clans, fostering religious unity.
Holy Fire Pavilion
A grand, semi-permanent structure of stone and wood, sheltering an eternal fire tended by a priestly order. Pilgrims now travel from afar, strengthening religious authority and unity.
Blessed Sanctuary
A stone-walled, richly adorned sanctuary with dedicated quarters for priests, facilities for pilgrims, and a sanctified altar for the Atash Behram. It radiates faith across the steppes.
Zoroastrian Fire Temple

A monumental and enduring fire temple built in the nomadic tradition, with stone walls, domed roofs, and a sanctified inner chamber holding the eternal flame. The temple serves as the supreme center of faith and unity for all clans of the steppes.
